subject: Career
title: White Space and Visual Hierarchy
description: One-minute skill: White Space and Visual Hierarchy.

hook.text: A wall of text triggers an instant 'no.' Recruiters need breathing room to scan.

buildup.text: Visual hierarchy guides the eye: headings, bold titles, and consistent spacing create order.

discovery.text: White space isn't wasted space. It signals confidence and makes key details pop.

twist.text: Cramming more content backfires. When everything fights for attention, nothing wins.

climax.text: The best resumes look effortless because someone spent hours editing down.

punchline.text: Less text, more impact. Let the page breathe.

quiz.question: Why is white space important on a resume?
options: It guides scanning and makes key details pop

details.summary: White space and visual hierarchy guide the reader's eye to your most important information. Strategic use of margins, spacing, bold text, and section ordering creates a scannable document that communicates hierarchy without requiring the reader to search.
details.whyItMatters: Dense, cluttered resumes are visually overwhelming and get abandoned during the six-second scan. Proper white space increases readership and comprehension of your key qualifications.
takeaways: Use adequate margins and spacing between sections for breathing room
Bold job titles and company names to create clear visual landmarks
Most important information should sit highest on the page

faq.question: How much white space should a well-formatted resume have?
faq.answer: Use half-inch to one-inch margins and add a line of space between major sections. Approximately thirty to forty percent of the page should be white space. If your resume feels dense when you squint at it, increase spacing. Readability is more valuable than cramming in extra content.

faq.question: Does resume visual design matter as much when ATS will parse it first?
faq.answer: Yes, because a human will see it eventually. After passing ATS screening, your resume is reviewed by a person who will judge it visually. Both ATS compatibility and human readability are required. Use simple formatting that satisfies both requirements simultaneously.
